rounds.text: Lykis Ltd carries severe financial vulnerabilities and severe leverage risks that undermine its superficial valuation appeal. Operating cash flow for Mar 2026 is deeply negative at Rs -13 Cr, resulting in an alarming cash conversion of -3.25x and leaving free cash flow at Rs -13 Cr [E34, E35, E36]. This cash burn is exacerbated by a dangerous surge in borrowings to Rs 77 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 34 Cr a year earlier, driving the debt-to-equity ratio to 2.14x where debt actively exceeds net worth [E38, E39]. Growth momentum has also severely stalled, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of -15%, a 3-year compounded profit growth of -28%, and zero compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E16, E20, E17]. Furthermore, structural profitability is weak with a low 3-year average return on equity of 6.83%, a 10-year median ROE of just 1%, and significant contingent liabilities totaling Rs 38.6 Cr alongside non-operating support from Rs 4.31 Cr in other income [E59, E26, E60, E61]. Extreme historical volatility of 63.9% and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -87.5% highlight the substantial downside risks embedded in this equity [E52, E51]. Conceded: [E43].
